title: Queen's Indian Defense: the ideas
line: The bishop on the long diagonal and the knight hold a key center square.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its queen two squares, into the center.
Bring the knight out. For now it stops White's other center pawn from coming to e4.
Move the pawn in front of your king one square. It opens a path for your bishop.

also.g7g6: That leads to the King's Indian, also sound. This lesson goes on with the other pawn.

steps.after: White brings out the other knight first, so a bishop on b4 would pin nothing.

steps.text: Move the pawn on b7 one square, to make room for your other bishop.

also.f8b4: That is the Bogo-Indian Defense, also sound. This lesson goes on with the other pawn.
also.d7d5: That holds the center with a pawn, also sound. This lesson goes on with the other pawn.

steps.after: This is the Queen's Indian Defense.

steps.text: Put the bishop on the long diagonal. With the knight, it watches e4.
steps.after: White pushes the pawn to e4 anyway. That is a mistake, not the usual move.

steps.text: White slipped. Your knight and bishop attack the pawn, and only one White knight guards it. Take it with the knight.

steps.after: Black is a pawn up, and the bishop sits in the center.

summary: The bishop on the long diagonal and the knight hold the center. A White pawn that comes too early falls.
